issues.legal_issue: Shares held by a company vest in the acquiring authority when they are connected with and held for the benefit of an acquired undertaking.
material_facts: The company’s textile business was its only business, and its six textile undertakings were interconnected.
Investments in the disputed shares were made from income or funds of the textile undertaking.
The shares were held or used for the benefit of the textile business, including as security for liabilities connected with the undertaking.
The company’s net wealth, excluding the disputed shares, was negative at the time of the takeover.
issues.conclusion: The disputed shares vested in the Central Government and, on transfer to the National Textile Corporation, the Corporation was entitled to them.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(k), 3 and 4(1) of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1986, read together, define the acquired undertakings broadly and extend vesting to the company’s rights and interests related to them. The expressions “pertaining to,” “in relation to” and “arising out of” are expansive; the inclusive deeming provision enlarges the scope of the vesting provision. Sections 7 and 8, which address contribution and compensation, do not determine which assets vest. The Court applied the ordinary meaning of clear statutory words, read in context and consistently with Article 39(b) and (c) of the Constitution. It distinguished Balkrishan Gupta v. Swadeshi Polytex Ltd., which concerned a takeover of management rather than acquisition of the undertaking, and relied on National Textile Corporation v. Sitaram Mills, Minerva Mills v. Union of India, Goverdhan Das Narasingh Das Daga v. Union of India, Vidharba Mills Berar Ltd. v. Union of India and Fine Knitting Co. Ltd. v. Union of India.

predicates.nationalisation_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns whether a company’s property passed to an authority under legislation acquiring an undertaking.
predicates.shares_bought_from_undertaking_income: The company acquired the shares using income or funds generated by the undertaking.
predicates.shares_held_for_undertaking_benefit: The company held or used the shares for the benefit of the undertaking.
predicates.related_shares_vest_in_acquiring_authori: Shares connected with and held for the benefit of an acquired undertaking pass to the acquiring authority.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding concerns shares bought from an undertaking’s income and held for its benefit, the shares pass to the acquiring authority.

issues.legal_issue: Immovable property owned or controlled by a company vests in the acquiring authority when it is related to an acquired undertaking.
material_facts: The bungalow and administrative block were immovable properties associated with the textile undertaking.
The properties were among the property whose vesting was disputed in proceedings concerning acquisition of the undertaking.
issues.conclusion: The bungalow and administrative block vested in the National Textile Corporation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4(1) of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1986, read with the definition in section 2(k), extend vesting to property and rights connected with the textile undertakings. The Court treated the expressions “pertaining to” and “in relation to” as broad terms and applied the clear statutory language in context. Its approach to statutory construction relied on Chandavarkar S.R. Rao v. Asha Lata and the principle that clear statutory words are ordinarily given their natural meaning.

predicates.nationalisation_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns whether a company’s property passed to an authority under legislation acquiring an undertaking.
predicates.company_owned_or_controlled_immovable_pr: The company owned or controlled the immovable property immediately before the acquisition took effect.
predicates.immovable_property_related_to_undertakin: The immovable property was related to the undertaking being acquired.
predicates.related_immovable_property_vests_in_acqu: Immovable property related to an acquired undertaking passes to the acquiring authority.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding concerns immovable property owned or controlled by a company and related to an acquired undertaking, the property passes to the acquiring authority.

issues.legal_issue: Documents prepared for Cabinet consideration need not be produced when they are irrelevant to construing clear statutory language and are protected as Cabinet papers.
material_facts: A party sought production of government documents, including papers prepared for Cabinet consideration, to support its interpretation of the acquisition legislation.
The Court found that the statutory provisions could be construed from their language and that the requested documents were not relevant to that construction.
The requested papers formed part of the preparation of advice tendered to the President through the Cabinet process.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the application for production and disclosure of the documents.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the requested documents were not relevant aids to construction where the statutory language was clear. It also held that Article 74(2) of the Constitution prevented inquiry into ministerial advice to the President and that papers prepared for Cabinet consideration were protected by their class, not merely by their contents. The Court relied on S.P. Gupta v. Union of India, State of U.P. v. Raj Narain, Sanjeev Coke Manufacturing Company v. Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. and State of Bihar v. Kripalu Shankar.

rule.if: statutory_interpretation_proceeding and cabinet_preparation_papers_requested and (statutory_words_resolve_dispute or papers_form_part_of_presidential_advice)

predicates.statutory_interpretation_proceeding: The proceeding requires the court to construe statutory language to decide a dispute.
predicates.cabinet_preparation_papers_requested: A party asked the court to order production of papers prepared for Cabinet consideration.
predicates.statutory_words_resolve_dispute: The statutory wording, read in context, provides a basis to resolve the dispute without relying on the requested papers.
predicates.papers_form_part_of_presidential_advice: The requested papers formed part of the process for preparing advice tendered to the President.

issues.definition: In a statutory interpretation proceeding, production is denied when Cabinet preparation papers are requested and either the statutory words resolve the dispute or the papers form part of advice tendered to the President.

issues.legal_issue: Formal rectification of a share register is unnecessary when shares are transmitted by operation of law and the register is to record the resulting ownership.
material_facts: The shares vested in the acquiring authority by operation of the acquisition legislation.
The Court directed that the company record the National Textile Corporation as shareholder instead of the former holders.
issues.conclusion: Rectification was unnecessary because the transmission of the shares occurred by operation of law.
issues.legal_principle: Applying section 108 of the Companies Act, 1956, the Court treated the vesting as a transmission of shares by operation of law, for which formal rectification was unnecessary. It also referred to Palmer’s Company Law, Mahadeo Lal Agarwala v. New Darjeeling Union Tea Co. Ltd. and Unity Company Pvt. Ltd. v. Diamond Sugar Mills.

predicates.share_transmission_dispute: The proceeding concerns recording a change in the holder of shares.
predicates.shares_transmitted_by_operation_of_law: The shares passed to a new holder automatically by operation of law rather than by a voluntary transfer.
predicates.register_entry_required_for_new_holder: The company’s register must record the person who acquired the shares by that transmission.
predicates.formal_register_rectification_not_requir: A separate formal rectification process is unnecessary to record a share transmission by operation of law.

issues.definition: When a share transmission dispute concerns shares passed by operation of law and a register entry for the new holder, formal rectification is unnecessary.
